items.title: Strong quantitative typing characterizes strong normalization and perpetual evaluation in the functional machine calculus
items.author: Willem Heijltjes
items.source_version: Fixed arXiv2505.09960v1 extended version; complete native TeX and appendicesB-F retrieved2026-10-13; publisher FSCD2025.24 is the conference version of the same work
items.difficulty_reason: The author relates non-idempotent quantitative derivations to effectful stack-machine reduction, proves weighted strong subject reduction, and constructs perpetual evaluation via a lexicographic reduction-length/term-size induction. The converse then reconstructs strong typeability by induction over every perpetual-evaluation case, including the admissible memory typing rules. All original derivations in the extended proof appendices are retained. This is non-routine H2; no H3 upgrade is inferred from the paper venue.
